questions.qtext: How many ways can you choose 4 groups of 4 people from 16 people, assuming the groups are distinct (i.e. group A, group B, group C, group D)?

Answer: 63063000
Source solution 3 (score: 1)
This is also a problem based on DODB (Distinguishable Objects into Distinguishable Boxes).

Basically here, we are distributing 16 distinct objects into 4 distinct boxes where each box contains 4 distinct objects each.

The number of ways in which this can be done is (16!)/(4!*4!*4!*4!) = 63063000.



In general, the number of ways in which k distinct objects can be distributed into n distinct boxes where the 1st box contains p1 objects, 2nd box contains p2 objects, 3rd box contains p3 objects,.............., nth box contains pN objects = (k!)/(p1!*p2!*p3!*.....*pN!) where (p1 + p2 + p3 +.......+ pN) = k.
